value.meaning: The SideFX API as declared authority. Every operation resolves to a declared capability, a kernel command operation or a view of a run the frontdoor admitted, and returns its declared output unchanged; the frontdoor that hosts the API carries this authority in its own declaration, reads no interface from the estate it serves, and carries no meaning of its own.

user.cookieWritesMeaning: A browser carries its session cookie to any request, so a cookie-carried write is admitted only when its Origin host is the workspace host, the request is not cross-site and its body is JSON. Bearer callers are not affected.
user.sessionRecheckMeaning: An open event stream of a session caller ends at the session expiry the identity host reports, and at the first recheck, this often, that cannot confirm the session.

readCache.meaning: A read operation that declares a cache is served from it for its time to live; concurrent reads of one request share one kernel call, and refresh=1 reads again. The bounds are the circuit host's read cache, which these reads replace.

limits.telemetryMeaning: A read operation that names its telemetry reports one span and one sfx.reader.duration point under that name per read, with its outcome and never its input or output. The names are the circuit host's reader names, which these reads replace.

value.inputTemplate: An operation input is a template. A string that begins with $caller., $path., $query. or $header. names that request value (a header by its lower-case name, as the ingress returns it) and $body names the request document; a named value the request does not carry omits its member. Every other value is literal.

operations.meaning: Admit a run of a declared capability: object, operation, subject, namespace, input and an optional idempotencyKey in the body or the Idempotency-Key header (both given, they must agree). The run store registers the run under the caller session and mints its id (the same key from the same caller names the same run, and a different submission under it is refused IDEMPOTENCY_KEY_CONFLICT); the answer is 202 with the run, and the host executes the run on a worker kernel, streams its observations and completes it in the run store when it ends. A caller without a live session is refused (EVIDENCE_SESSION_REQUIRED).
Read the state of a run from the run store: state, exit code, timing, output availability and graphs.
Read the retained trace chunks of a run.

Stream the events of a run of the caller as server-sent events: each event after the cursor (after, or Last-Event-ID) as id, event and data, each new event as the run writes it, then an end event with the run state and last cursor once the run has ended and been completed.
Read the output of a run from the run store.
Read the delivery a run was admitted on: language, delivery, mode and the eligibility that selected it.
Read the execution graphs of a run, one per execution root.
Read a run of the caller from the run store: state, material and trust.
Read the retained trace chunks of a run of the caller.
Compile the declared composition of a capability and return its execution-graph projection; no run is admitted.
List the capabilities of the estate (list-capabilities): id, namespace, definition digest, mode, root scenario, scenario count, user story, promise and circuit availability.
Read the live scenario circuit of a capability.
Read the details of a capability: every set, navigation included.
Read a declared UI page.
Read a declared standards crosswalk.
Read the declared inspection of a provider: every result set of the provider inspection with its name, columns and rows.

The estates the caller may open in Estate (the selected estate when its scope is readable), with how their retained and live activity are read. The legacy circuit host derived this from an admitted topology run; here the reader runs inside the read and no run is created.

The selected estate topology: capability identities with their selected-definition revisions and admitted capability-to-capability relationships, within the legacy bounds (500 capabilities, 2000 relationships).

Execution activity in an interval of at most 24 hours (start, end) as of an instant (asOf, the playback time or the interval end): admitted (runId, rootExecutionId) instances with their own-outcome states, counts, coverage and cursor. The reader refuses an empty, reversed or longer interval.
Execution capture coverage: source states and watermarks, fact kinds, explicit gaps, withheld conflicts and admissions missing their ingress block.
Invocation provenance of up to 200 instances: captured ingress and its classification, parentage and correlation.
The revision basis of up to 200 instances: the captured authority revision against the selected definition digest, with explicit mismatch states.

Watch the estate live: subscribe to the estate's live observation channel, every execution the host publishes and every circuit drawing change the estate reads (kind drawing-change, payload estate-drawing-change.v1), as server-sent events of the observer record ({seq, observationKey, receivedAt, kind, runId, api, glyph, cls, text, payload}) framed by publish-estate-live-observation, through subscribe-estate-live-observation. since (or Last-Event-ID) replays the retained channel after that sequence; without it only new publications arrive; a refused selector answers 400 invalid_run, invalid_since or invalid_bound. bound (whole seconds) ends the stream that long after it opens, unless the session ends first. The x-observer-instance header names the channel; a new instance began a new sequence. The stream ends at the caller session expiry and at the first recheck that cannot confirm the session. The same subscription as GET /events.

The legacy observer's subscription at its own path, outside the API prefix, for the subscribers built against it (the machine watchers and routers, the Explorer's live circuit, the Fractal Lab bridge): the same channel, selectors and record as /sfx/v1/estate-execution/stream, through subscribe-estate-live-observation.

The legacy circuit host's run output path, outside the API prefix, for the subscribers that read a run's output when its run-end reaches the feed (the machine watchers and routers): the same read as /sfx/v1/runs/{runId}/output.
Sign in: served by the ingress, so the credential never reaches the frontdoor.
Read the caller session as the authenticated ingress resolved it: kind, principal, session and expiry.
Sign out: sfx-identity revokes the caller session.
Read the host's execution profile: the exact bytes of the profile this deployment promises, and their SHA-256.

closure.responsibility: the kernel identifies the caller, resolves the request against the interface its declaration carries, and runs the operation's capability
